title: Auth Control Plane principal (v1 wire format)
description:
The resolved principal the Auth Control Plane hands to a relying party once a credential has been verified. This is a WIRE contract: the JSON Schema, the OpenAPI document that references it, and the golden fixtures under contracts/auth/v1/examples/principal/ are the source of truth, and the Go/Python/TypeScript types are implementations of it, never the other way round.

Distinct from contracts/auth/v1/endpoint-profiles.ops.json and credential-classes.json, which are the Wave 0 INVENTORY contract describing what authentication exists today. This file describes what the new service emits. Neither constrains the other, and this file changes nothing about them.

DELIBERATE OMISSION, load-bearing: there is no `tier` and no `licensed_features`. ACP-ADR-07 decision 2 (Accepted 2026-09-02) states that entitlement is an input to a decision and never a claim in a credential, and deprecates both fields from the effective-principal envelope's claim schema at its next `v` bump; G-14 forbids entitlement travelling inside a credential by name. The existing envelope carries them today (cmd/query-api/internal/principal/claims.go), so a reader comparing this schema against that struct will find two fields missing and must not `fix` it -- their absence IS the ADR. Entitlement reaches a relying party through the authorization decision, not through the principal.

schema_version.description: Identifies this document's contract. A relying party MUST reject an unrecognised value rather than parse optimistically (ACP-ADR-05 decision 1: unknown denies). Note this is NOT the effective-principal envelope's `v` claim -- see the `v`-vs-`.v1` note on `token_version`.

principal_id.description: Stable opaque identifier for the acting principal. For principal_type `human` this is the user id and corresponds to the existing envelope's `sub` claim. Opaque to relying parties: never parse it, never infer type from its shape.

principal_type.description: Which kind of principal is acting. This enum is REUSED VERBATIM from contracts/auth/v1/credential-classes.schema.json ($defs.credentialClass.properties.principal_type), the Wave 0 closed vocabulary covering all 30 frozen credential classes -- it is deliberately not a new vocabulary. A seventh kind is a change to that file first and this one second, never here alone.

organization_id.description: Tenant this principal is acting within. null ONLY for a principal that is genuinely org-less (an `infrastructure` principal acting on the platform itself). A relying party that scopes by organization MUST treat null as `no organization` and deny, never as `any organization` -- ACP-ADR-12 decision 3 makes org-scoped-from-claims the default idiom precisely so a caller-supplied organization is unrepresentable rather than merely rejected.

role.description: Coarse role name where the principal has one, null otherwise. Present for continuity with the current model and for audit legibility. It is NOT an authorization input: ACP-ADR-05 decision 4 requires an explicit action name at the call site and forbids an `is_admin`-style check as the final decision (G-27). Authorize on `permissions`, or on an authorization decision; never on this field.

permissions.description: The principal's resolved action set, sorted, from the registered closed action vocabulary (ACP-ADR-05 decision 1). Unknown action denies. An empty array is a valid, meaningful value -- an authenticated principal that may do nothing -- and MUST NOT be treated as `unrestricted` or as `not populated`.

items.description: A dotted, namespaced action name: `members.invite`, `acr.context.read`, `billing.subscription.manage` (ACP-ADR-05 decision 4). At least two segments is deliberate -- a single bare segment is the shape of the `is_admin` check G-27 exists to forbid, so the pattern makes it unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.

is_superuser.description: The principal holds the platform superuser bit. On its own this is a CLAIM, not an authorization: pair it with is_superuser_verified, which is the half that carries current-state evidence.

is_superuser_verified.description: The superuser bit was re-verified against current state when this principal was resolved, rather than carried forward from an earlier decision. A relying party performing a cross-organization or otherwise superuser-gated action MUST require this to be true (threat model 3.2's current-state check). is_superuser true with is_superuser_verified false is a legitimate, expressible state and means `claimed but unverified` -- deny the superuser-gated path on it.

token_version.description: The principal's credential-generation counter; a bump invalidates previously issued credentials for this principal. Distinct from `schema_version` above and from the effective-principal envelope's `v` claim -- three different version-shaped numbers exist in this system and conflating them is the trap: `v`/`schema_version` version the CONTRACT, `token_version` versions the PRINCIPAL'S CREDENTIALS, and the `.v1` in this file's name versions the API SURFACE.

impersonation.description: Active impersonation context, or null when the principal is acting as itself. Never omitted -- the key is REQUIRED and explicitly null, so `absent` cannot be confused with `not impersonating` by a consumer whose deserializer defaults a missing object to a zero value.

impersonated_by.description: principal_id of the operator acting AS this principal. The surrounding principal_id/organization_id/role remain the TARGET's identity, matching the current issuer's behaviour; this field is the only place the operator appears.

started_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which the impersonation session began. CROSS-LANGUAGE NOTE: `format` is carried for semantics and IS asserted by the Python and TypeScript validators, but github.com/google/jsonschema-go states in its own doc.go ("Deviations from the specification") that `format` is recorded and then IGNORED during validation -- it does not even produce an annotation -- and recommends `pattern` instead. The `pattern` beside it is therefore the cross-language FLOOR that all three validators enforce identically; `format` is the stricter calendar check the two that support it apply on top. Never rely on `format` alone in these schemas: it would be enforced in two languages out of three, which is the drift class the cross-language goldens exist to catch. The digit class is written [0-9] and NEVER \d: Python's `re` treats \d as UNICODE and accepts Arabic-Indic and Devanagari digits, while Go RE2 and ECMA-262 treat it as ASCII only -- MEASURED, not assumed: the Devanagari timestamp in examples/principal/invalid-expires-at-unicode-digits.json was accepted by the Python validator and rejected by the Go one under the \d spelling. Same hazard for \w and \s. Always use an explicit character class in these schemas.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry of the impersonation session. ACP-ADR-03 fixes the delegated/impersonation session at 15 minutes and independently revocable -- shorter than the base session (G-52). This bound is independent of the enclosing principal's own expires_at and neither one widens the other. revisions.description: The monotonic revisions this principal was resolved against. ACP-ADR-05 decision 3 requires policy_revision in every decision and requires every allow-cache key to bind membership, grant and entitlement revisions alongside it (G-31), so that a revision bump invalidates by construction rather than by an explicit purge. A consumer that caches anything derived from this principal MUST include all four values in its cache key.

entitlement_revision.description: The entitlement projection revision this resolution saw. This is a CACHE-INVALIDATION input, not an entitlement value -- it says which snapshot was current, never what it granted. Carrying the revision here is what lets a consumer bind its cache correctly without the principal carrying entitlement itself, which ACP-ADR-07 decision 2 forbids.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which this principal document was resolved. expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry. ACP-ADR-03 sets the bounds per credential class and states that the effective-principal envelope's per-call TTL override is REMOVED: a security bound any call site may widen is not a bound. Relying parties MUST enforce this and MUST NOT accept an issuer-supplied extension. issuer.description: Issuing authority. A verifier MUST require a non-empty expected issuer -- an empty expected value disables issuer checking outright in at least one widely used JWT library (see NewVerifier's doc comment in cmd/query-api/internal/principal/verifier.go), which fails open rather than closed.

audience.description: Intended audience. Same fail-open hazard as issuer: an empty expected audience disables the check rather than failing it.
